# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009)</sub>
- **Status:** Single  <sub>[v2 c22 P5](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper at Ingleside  <sub>[v2 c11 P0](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0000), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v4 c2 P0](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan Baker is an elderly spinster with a grim, gaunt appearance. She admits to not being a beauty and considers herself plain-looking. In her own words, she is no beauty, but feels she looks as good as most married women.

_Sources: [v2 c11 P0](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0000), [v2 c22 P5](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0005), [v3 c33 P15](../source/v03-c33.md#nw-v03-c33-p0015), [v4 c2 P0](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0000)_

## Personality

Susan is a fiercely loyal, hardworking, and practical woman who takes immense pride in her household duties. Though grim and outspoken, she possesses a deeply tender and affectionate heart, especially toward the children in her care. She holds strong, traditional, and occasionally superstitious opinions, yet remains fiercely protective of her loved ones. She takes great satisfaction in cooking for those who appreciate her meals and approaches her work with calm efficiency.

_Sources: [v2 c7 P0](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0000), [v2 c11 P0](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0000), [v2 c21 P1](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0001), [v2 c22 P5](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0005), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c36 P5](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0005), [v4 c19 P1](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0001), [v4 c19 P11](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0011)_

## History

Susan Baker was employed as the housekeeper at Green Gables and later moved to Ingleside with Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne. When Anne fell severely ill after the birth of her son Shirley, Susan nursed and cared for the baby, claiming him as her own and developing an intense maternal devotion to him. She managed the Ingleside household with dedication, keeping it in order and preparing meals for the family. Susan remained a steadfast presence through all the joys and sorrows of the Blythe family, including the tragic loss of Anne's firstborn child, Joy. When Anne and Gilbert moved from their house of dreams to the Glen St. Mary home, Susan cheerfully accompanied them to manage their larger residence.

_Sources: [v2 c7 P0](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0000), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P11](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0011), [v4 c2 P0](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0000), [v4 c19 P1](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0001), [v4 c19 P11](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0011), [v4 c40 P43](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0043)_
